sentences.text: Muthineni Veeranna vs Head Constable865 on 8 July, 2025

Author: N.Tukaramji
Bench: N.Tukaramji
 The Honourable Sri Justice N.Tukaramji
 Criminal Petition No. 8378 Of 2025
Order

This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS, 2023') seeking quashment of the proceedings in Crime No.268 of 2025 of P.S Narasampet Police Station, Warangal District, against the petitioner/accused.

entities.text: P.S Narasampet Police Station, Warangal District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. The petitioner is arrayed as accused No.1 in Crime No.268 of 2025 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 272, 275 of BNS.

3. Heard Ms.C.Sunitha Kumari, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr.Jithender Rao Veeramalla, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, representing the respondents.
4.

The prosecution case in brief is that the petitioner/accused is involved in selling and purchasing the banned Tobacco products and the Police concerned has seized the said Tobacco products worth of Rs.1,88,300/- from the possession of the petitioner.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that a Coordinate Bench of this Court vide Criminal Petition Nos.3731 and Batch on considering similar allegations and the merits quashed the proceedings against the petitioner therein.
He further submits that the police have 2 NTR,J registered the present crime in violation of the orders passed by this Court.
Hence, prayed for quashment of the proceedings against the petitioner.
6. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor would submit that the petitioner has been found with the Tobacco products and investigation is pending.
However fairly admitted that in the authority cited by the petitioner in the similar circumstances, the proceedings against the petitioner therein were quashed.
7. I have perused the materials on record.

8. As per the prosecution, on 29.06.2025 at 13.00 hours, the complainant/head Constable lodged a complaint alleging that he along with his staff, reached Sarvapuram, Mahabubabad Road, Old Petrol bunk at 13:00 noon and while they were patrolling the vehicles, a person driving a Maruti Suzuki Eeco car number No.TS24-J-0419 saw them and stopped the car and tried to flee.
They immediately caught that person and seized the car.

It contained amber packets, RR packers and Anar packets Muthineni Veeranna vs Head Constable865 on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36570453/
1 banned by the Government.

The accused stated that the money earned from business was not enough to support his family, he wanted to earn a lot of money in an easy way with less investment,
so he bought Amber packets, RR packets and Anar packets banned by Government from a person named Prashant in Mahabubabad and sold them to the Kirana shops in the villages of Narsampet and earned high profits.
Accordingly, the complainant and his staff apprehended the petitioner and seized 3 NTR,J tobacco products 1)Amber 300-packets, worth of Rs.300 x 400 = Rs.1,35,000/-, 2)

RR Tobacco 88-packets, worth of Rs.88 x 350 = Rs.30,800/-, 3) Anar tobacco packets 50-packets,
worth of Rs.50 x 350 = Rs.17,500/- total worth of Rs.1,88,300/- under cover of panchanama.

9. It is pertinent to note that the related Notification No.501/FSS/I/2022 dated 07.01.2022,
prohibiting manufacturing, storing, distribution, transportation and sale of gutka and pan masala in the entire State of Telangana, has been stayed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Shri Venkateshwara Traders v. State of Telangana and others vide SLA No.20441 of 2021 with SLP(C)
No.1656 of 2022.

entities.text: Shri Venkateshwara Traders v. State of Telangana and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, the Director General of Police, Telangana State issued Circular Memorandum in RC.No. 295/R1-NS/2022 with directions to the Station House Officers not to interfere with the business activities, who carry out the business as per rules of Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and also not to take any coercive measures against the tobacco traders as long as the order of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is in force.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 10. Having regard to similar factual position, a Coordinate Bench of this Court in Crl.P.No.6235 of 2022 held that against the allegations of illegal sale and transportation of tobacco products the accusations under Sections 188, 269, 270, 272, 273, 278, 328 read with Sections 511, 336, 409 and 420 of I.P.C., cannot be maintained and quashed the proceedings against the petitioners therein.
4 NTR,J 11.
In the instant petition, the prosecution for possession and allegation of sale arraigned the offences under Sections 270, 273 of Indian Penal Code.
12. As noted above, the conclusions drawn in the earlier criminal petition are squarely measuring up the predicament in the present petition.
13. For that reason, the proceedings against the petitioner stand unsustainable.
Accordingly, this Criminal Petition deserves positive consideration.
14. Resultantly, the Criminal Petition is allowed.
The proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.1 in Crime No.268 of 2025 of P.S Narasampet Police Station, Warangal District are hereby quashed.

entities.text: P.S Narasampet Police Station, Warangal District
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner-accused No.1 is granted liberty to file appropriate application for return of seized property, whereupon the trail Court is directed to release the seized property to the petitioner on proper acknowledgment.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
